**Try the same-set counterexample after implementing `compare_logits`.** Copy this into a scratch code cell before reading its reveal:

```python
reference = t.arange(6, dtype=t.float32).reshape(1, 1, 6)
custom = 10 * reference
print(compare_logits(custom, reference, k=2))
```

<details><summary>Counterexample reveal and interpretation</summary>

Both top-2 sets are `{4,5}`, so agreement is 1, while max absolute logit error is 45, MSE is 742.5, and mean KL(reference || custom) is approximately 4.64746. Scaling preserves ranks but sharpens probability concentration. Thus top-k agreement cannot replace distributional tolerances. This is a hand-checkable synthetic metric fixture, not real-model parity. A categorical confidence is a subjective event probability; a numeric forecast should instead give a value/range and units.

</details>
